# Performance

Everything is read into memory, and the inputs are large: human release 116's GTF is 141 MB compressed (mzLib's EnsemblGeneSet remarks), and the vertebrate gene-tree file holds 4.2 million genes unless --restrict-gene-trees keeps only the given species'. For human, mouse and rat at release 116, mzLib \#1381 reports the build from the three dumps at about 20 s and the written snapshot (13 files, 9.0 MB) at about 40 s more. No call here takes a degree of parallelism, so there is no --threads.

# Not yet verified

The spec lists these as open; they are reported, never hidden:

- result.tables (gene\_sets, gene\_trees, dumps, pairs, written, pair\_status and the Parquet tables) is not validated by tools/check\_verbs.py, which checks only envelope\_fields, columns and bulk. Bridge tests pin each nested object's keys (GenesOrthologyTests).
- The Parquet tables' units are mzLib's doc comments (ComparaHomology: identity percent, goc\_score and wga\_coverage 0 to 100). dn and ds are written as dN and dS conventionally are, substitutions per site; neither mzLib nor this bridge has checked Compara's own definition.
- Only one pair-status direction per call, and no SpeciesSet tuples or ortholog rows on the wire: the written Parquet and views.sql answer those. Whether a binding needs them without a Parquet reader (pyMzLib has no third-party dependency) is open.
- source\_dump records the dump's file name, which Ensembl gives every species' dump (PUSH-TO-MAINLAND: mzLib could record the dump's genome, or the path under homologies/, beside it).
- Not yet ported to mzLibRust or mzLibR; the binding names above are proposals.
